_comment: Every error code the membership transaction can send to the editor.
The backend raises these as MembershipError; the dialog turns them into
copy a user can act on. The two sides live in different languages, so this
fixture is the contract between them — the same pattern curve_presets.json
already uses for the shape definitions.
`copy` says where the user-facing text comes from:
dedicated  - the dialog owns a specific string for this code, because the
backend message is not actionable enough on its own.
backend    - the dialog surfaces the backend message verbatim; the
backend message must therefore read as user-facing copy.
preferred  - the backend message wins when present (it names the entity),
and the dialog has its own string for when it is absent.
Adding a backend code without adding it here fails the Python contract test.
Adding it here without the dialog handling it fails the frontend one.

empty_selection.meaning: The submitted selection contained no lights.

duplicate.meaning: The same light appeared twice in the selection.

not_a_light.meaning: A submitted entity id is not in the light domain.

self_reference.meaning: The group was asked to control itself.

recursive_lightener.meaning: A submitted light is itself a Lightener group.

disabled_entity.meaning: A newly added light is disabled in Home Assistant.

not_found.meaning: The config entry or a submitted light no longer exists.

conflict.meaning: The group changed since the editor loaded it.

reload_failed.meaning: The write was rolled back; the previous state is intact.

rollback_reload_failed.meaning: The write failed and the previous runtime could not be restored.
